skeptic.argument: I went and looked instead of arguing. `src/screens/drafts.jsx` and `src/screens/labels.jsx` do not exist — pass 1 read them off a routing table that still lists routes the app stopped serving. The daily digest is a real thing but it is an email template, not a screen this lens can grade, and it has no path for the engine to check. All three should leave the inventory as phantom claims, checked where they can be checked.

builder.argument: Dropping three units is the one move in this system that can flatter the coverage number, so it should cost something. Two of these the engine can verify against disk; the digest it cannot, and that one should stay visibly marked as a claim nobody checked rather than quietly disappearing.

dreamer.argument: A routing table that lists two screens nobody built is its own finding about this codebase, but it is a finding about the router, and the router is not a unit in this inventory. Naming it here and letting it go is the honest move.

empath.argument: If drafts genuinely does not exist, then the compose autosave finding gets worse rather than better: the work is saved somewhere the reader has no screen to go and find. That is worth saying inside the compose finding itself.
